correctness.rationale: For alpha>1, the commuting finite-flip Hamiltonians converge in norm. Their Born laws factor as Bernoulli bits with probabilities sin^2(tck^(-alpha)); Hilbert-norm convergence implies total-variation convergence of the Born laws, and the independent product has finite support almost surely in the sense of finitely many occupied coordinates, since the probabilities sum. No division by a cosine is used. With N=(ct)^beta, the normalized mean is the Riemann sum of sin^2(x^(-alpha)); the oscillatory portion on (0,epsilon) is bounded by its interval length up to discretization and the tail is dominated by x^(-2alpha). Substitution v=2x^(-alpha) and integration by parts reduce the limiting integral to 2^(beta-1) times the sine transform of v^(-beta), giving the claimed gamma-cosine value for 0<beta<1. The variance identity V_t=mu_(2t)/4 fixes the factor 2^(beta-2). For centered Bernoulli variables sum of third absolute moments is at most V_t; finite Berry–Esseen passes to the countable sum by L^2 convergence at each t and continuity of the Gaussian CDF, giving O(V_t^(-1/2)). Chebyshev gives the stated concentration since V_t/mu_t^2 tends to zero.
residual_risks: Reported finite numerical truncations are diagnostic only. The rate is an upper bound for the standardized single-time law, not a sharp rate or a process-level limit.

value.rationale: Graph distance is a natural transport observable for this infinite weighted model, and the complete power-law scaling separates the spreading exponent, its dimensional prefactor and the asymptotic variance-to-mean ratio. Those quantities identify how spread and fluctuations depend on alpha and do not follow from existence of unitary dynamics or from the generic CLT alone. The contribution is the sharp model-specific calculation, not a new independent-sum limit theorem.
residual_risks: Conclusions concern the empty-set initial state, exact power-law weights with alpha>1 and one-time laws only.
